prerequisites: Mathematics: Calculus II and Differential Equations/V12G380V01204
To enroll in this course, it is necessary to have passed or be enrolled in all subjects from courses prior to the one in which this subject is located.

learning_outcomes.text: CG3 Knowledge in basic and technological subjects that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
CE11 Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.
Know the operation of electronic devices.
Know electronic systems for data conditioning and acquisition.
Identify the different types of industrial sensors.
Know electronic circuits for information communication.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Control and supervision of industrial systems by means of electronics
Electronic devices, circuits and systems: Electronic components and devices
Electronic devices, circuits and systems: Passive and active electronic devices
Electronic devices, circuits and systems: Analog and digital electronic circuits
Electronic devices, circuits and systems: Electronic systems
Diodes and rectification: The diode, operation and characteristics
Diodes and rectification: Types of diodes
Diodes and rectification: Analysis of circuits with diodes
Diodes and rectification: Rectification and filtering
Transistors: The bipolar transistor, operating principle and characteristic curves
Transistors: Calculation of the bias point
Transistors: The transistor as an amplifier
Amplification: Some basic configurations with Op-Amp
Digital Electronics I: Combinational functions. Analysis, synthesis, simplification
Electronic Sensors: Types of sensors based on the magnitudes to be measured
Electronic Sensors: Some sensors of special interest in industry
Electronic Sensors: Electrical equivalent of some typical sensors
Electronic Sensors: Study of some cases of sensor-ADC coupling
Analog-to-Digital Converters: Analog signals and digital signals
Analog-to-Digital Converters: Sampling, quantification and digitalization
Analog-to-Digital Converters: Most relevant characteristics of ADCs: number of bits, speed, conversion range and cost
Power Electronics: Linear and switching power supplies
teaching_methods: Prior study (preparation for theoretical sessions and lab practices)
assessment_rules: The final grade (NA) is calculated as 30% from the lab exam (NL) and 70% from the theory grade (NT). To pass, both NL and NT must be 3.3/10 or higher; otherwise, the maximum final grade is capped at 4.8/10, and a final score of 5 points is required. The theory grade (NT) can be obtained through partial exams (P1+P2) or a single comprehensive exam (EC) in ordinary or extraordinary calls. Unethical behavior or use of unauthorized electronic devices during exams will result in a 0.0 grade for the entire course.
